text: Second, it makes room for the views of the non-religious community.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Both religiosity and secularism are growing in Singapore and the region.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Many in this group do hold the controversial view that religion is irrational and not beneficial to society.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: It matters that both the non-religious minority and the religious majority learn how to uncover their commonalities and also discuss their differences with compassion.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Third, it goes beyond building inter-religion to intra-religion understanding as well.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: There is a dangerous lack of conversations between conservatives, moderates and liberals within the same religion.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Religious teachers do not typically initiate engagement of leaders from their own community on the opposite spectrum for fear of looking like they are softening their standards.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Such a conversation needs to be encouraged by outsiders as well as insiders.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: When we create safe spaces where we can be honest about the differences that we disagree over and yet open towards the commonalities that bind, we will reap true religious harmony.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: According to the Centre of the Developing Child at Harvard, the best way to understand how we develop resilience is to visualise a see-saw.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: On one side sits positive experiences, coping skills and at least one stable committed adult relationship.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: The more protective experiences, coping skills and strong relationships we provide, the more we can counterbalance the piling on of adversity on the other end.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: It is this holy trinity that develops resilience in a child and no singular organisation can achieve this effectively by itself.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: When Minister Heng Swee Keat shared about having bespoke plans for the industrial transformation of more than 20 specific economic sectors in Singapore, it struck me.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: Do we also have bespoke plans for the generational transformation of, say, 20 or more specific archetypes of youths?

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: The sector is still fragmented and working in silos.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
text: I believe the sharing of such a roadmap will help all of us stakeholders within the youth sector to know our place in the resilience value chain and thus realise how to collaborate more effectively for our common goal.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Chairman, as we write the next chapters for the next 50 years of Singapore, we will need to look at how, as a mature society, we handle diversity of views.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Diversity can be a strength if energies can be synergised and used for the good of the people.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, it is also a potential divisive factor that can tear our social fabric.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I am particularly concerned that we are starting to see vitriolic debates and conversations happening in the online space.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I understand that these toxic exchanges do not necessarily reflect the current state of affairs offline or the mentality of the larger majority.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, I cannot help but worry that such airing of views reflects the unspoken thoughts of many.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I am also concerned that the young, who grow up exposed to and dependent on information they obtain from the Internet may be impacted by the views online.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The SGFuture engagements have also been an excellent platform for discussions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We need to engage youths on matters that are important to them, especially since they will inherit the nation and should have a say in how the society develops.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Beyond creating the platforms and spaces for them to interact, for there to be real discourse, I believe there also needs to be opportunities for more open debates and discussions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I would, therefore, like to ask what specific measures the Ministry would take in ensuring meaningful social mixing, interactions and discussions through the youth activities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: What more can be done to ensure a sustainable and continued engagement and interaction among youths from diverse backgrounds, beyond just the activities which they participate in?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Our call for embracing diversity and maintaining our multireligious and multicultural values need to go beyond platitudes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We need to make diversity our strength and not cause our fall.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I have faith that we will be able to achieve this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But there needs to be effort by all to make a constant and conscious effort to encourage and embrace diversity.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Chairman, while we can debate the role of education or parenting in growing young people with strength and fortitude, I believe that experiential learning is critical to developing our youths holistically in this area.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The experience of being in a natural setting, away from urban familiarity, to have one's physical and mental abilities stretched to the fullest, should be offered to all Singaporean youths.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Indeed, I was just at OBS on Pulau Ubin few days ago on Sunday and just being there for few hours really helped alleviate pressures of being in an urban environment and brought back fond memories also of my time in OBS.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: One element of National Service which is important is the social mixing that it involves.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Singaporeans of all races, religions, socio-economic groups and educational backgrounds get to mix together, and this strengthens and enhances the social fabric of our community.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: And those from a Special Assistance Plan (SAP) school could go for OBS with unique schools like School of the Arts or even NorthLight.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: While this would require some logistics and planning, I believe that it would also be beneficial as students now not only get stretched physically and mentally, they also get to develop their emotional quotient and empathy by learning how to interact and cooperate with other young Singaporeans who are different from them.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: In addition to continuing their collaboration with MOE, I hope that MCCY can share with the House how we can all work together to create a new generation of Singaporeans who are physically and mentally tougher and ready to accept any challenge that comes their way.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Mr Chairman, I still remember the experience I had at OBS when I was in secondary school.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It was especially memorable because I was from an all-girls' school and it was my first time interacting with boys of the same age, solving problems and battling the rugged outdoors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It was also an opportunity for girls to push their physical limits, challenge their fears and bond with students from other schools and other races, especially since girls do not serve National Service.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is, therefore, critical for parents to buy in and support this initiative in order to ensure that it successfully achieves its objectives.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can the Ministry provide greater details of the activities that OBS will embark on and what it tries to achieve?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: If in their daily interactions with their children, parents are able to compliment and reinforce what OBS sets out to achieve, we are more likely to achieve longer-term benefits of this programme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Also, in order to maintain the quality of the OBS experience for students, can the Ministry take steps to educate students ahead of the programme so that all will do it with the right attitude and enthusiasm?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: OBS has, in the past, been seen as a star programme for student leaders.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Even as it is now made available to all, the experience of the programme should be upheld and all students should come away from it feeling proud of themselves and their achievements.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Dr Goh's vision was for OBS to help build a rugged society.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: True to his vision, the fundamental philosophy underlining the operations of OBS has not changed over the past nearly 50 years.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: I am glad that OBS is now being expanded to strengthen our rugged society.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: At the official opening of Coney Island, Minister Khaw Boon Wan said in his speech, "We will, of course, keep the island rustic and keep to its natural state, as much as possible.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Coney Island is home to a wide variety of habitats, including coastal forests, grasslands and mangroves.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: I would still like to ask what are the measures taken to minimise the impact to the environment and how the rustic nature of the island can be preserved.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Many are doing well in diverse fields, such as business, the arts and information technology (IT).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: More encouragingly, we see more students take on courses in high demand areas, such as food science, biological science and information and communications technology (ICT).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: More Malays are also getting married but there are fewer minor marriages and remarriages.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Future of Us Exhibition and SGfuture conversations are important touchpoints where we can share our hopes, ideas and aspirations to co-create our future together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am glad to see many of our youths participating in this endeavour.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have 27-year-old Khairul Rusydi, co-founder of Reactor, an educational technology company.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: He aspires to illuminate alternative pathways to success for youths.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Since participating in the inaugural SGfuture session, he worked with the National Youth Council to spearhead the SGfuture engagement on the Future Economy in March, which explored ways to ensure Singapore remains economically vibrant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This weekend, Rusydi, together with Reactor, will spearhead a session on the Future of Youth Entrepreneurship to encourage the exchange of innovative ideas and collaborations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our young will play a very important role and we have seen many young role models stepping forward and showcasing the best values of the community regardless of where they are.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: A group of young aspiring asatizahs studying in the University of Jordan distributed specially prepared packets of food to the poor, including street cleaners and the elderly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Back home, under the Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation, our youths in mosques and madrasahs worked together to bring joy, care and blessings to elderly residents in Ren Ci Nursing Home.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The trends and examples are part of a larger story, the story of the hard work put in by so many Malay/Muslims who are determined to forge a brighter future for themselves and their families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will continue to work together to lay the foundations to help bring out the best in Page: 9 everyone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These include Edusave, ComCare subsidies, Workfare and Community Health Assistance Scheme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Apart from the Industry Transformation Programme, Budget 2016 also offered key educational and social support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These include the First Step Grant for the Child Development Account; KidSTART, which will help level up disadvantaged children; and the Fresh Start Housing scheme to help families in rental flats own their own homes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The community is determined to progress and the foundations for its future are being laid with this Budget.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In this speech, I would like to address two key issues for the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, to ensure that our community is ready to seize the opportunities of a rapidly changing economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Second, to address a more diverse socio-religious landscape, for which we will need new strategies to counter extremist and exclusivist influences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I will also touch on ongoing efforts to build on the community's progress in education and its socio-religious life and to fine-tune efforts to strengthen families and better support the vulnerable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Against a backdrop of disruptive technologies, our industries need to transform and adapt.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Skills upgrading will be more important than ever and ICT will be a key enabler.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our young must recognise this and be ready for a job market where skills and experience will outweigh qualifications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zainal Sapari asked about the Unit's plans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, building on the Government's SGfuture engagement efforts, MENDAKI will reach out to the community through a series of Future Ready Conversations and NextStop engagements.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Conversations will help MENDAKI to better understand the hopes and aspirations of our community and how it can provide more targeted and effective support. "NextStop" is more targeted.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MENDAKI will engage students from secondary schools, the Institutes of Technical Education (ITEs) and polytechnics so that they have a better appreciation of the growth sectors in our economy and, relatedly, the range of academic and career pathways under SkillsFuture.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Second, the Unit will introduce Future Ready Mentoring for secondary level and ITE students.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Some of our students may not be well-informed of the available opportunities or may lack the confidence to pursue their aspirations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mentors will help broaden the perspectives of mentees and advise them on their choice of education and career pathways.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One key initiative would be the "Making SENSE of SkillsFuture" fairs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat was concerned about how we can better support our workforce facing short- to mid-term challenges.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MENDAKI SENSE has been offering a variety of courses and job matching services to those who need help.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This year, in addition to these, SENSE will also offer a Page: 10 number of free courses that support lifelong learning, career readiness and skills upgrading.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We already have a number of talented individuals in our community who have blazed a trail in this field.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Take, for example, Muhammad Danish bin Muhammad Imran.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This dynamic 21-year-old Ngee Ann Polytechnic graduate was the top student in his specialisation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As a child, his parents had exposed Danish to IT, and it has been his passion ever since.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In primary school, Danish built websites and, in secondary school, he worked on an app to help students learn better.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It was in polytechnic where his passion and strength converged.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There, Danish's participation in Microsoft's YouthSpark programme prompted him to develop an app called "Taxi Split".

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Based on his experience with sharing taxi fares with his friends who alight at different destinations, this app helped to calculate the exact taxi fare using game theory.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: He later shared his knowledge on creating computational thinking programmes with students and social enterprises, as part of his work as a YouthSpark coordinator for Microsoft Asia Pacific.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We want to spark the interest of more students who are like Danish.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will complement the efforts of schools in nurturing the interest and skills of students through technology-related learning activities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our socio-religious life has always been guided by principles of moderation, inclusiveness and respect for differences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our Pioneers, such as the late President Yusof Ishak, Allahyarham Ustaz Ahmad Sonhadji Mohamed, Allahyarham Pak Ridzwan Dzafir and Allahyarham Ustaz Ibrahim Kassim, exemplified these principles and worked hard to strengthen the social fabric of a multicultural and multi-religious Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our Pioneers have showed us how we can remain rooted to our traditions, values and principles and participate actively in our nation-building efforts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is up to us, therefore, to build upon their past efforts and nurture a cohesive and progressive Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And our Malay/Muslim community has been long used to diversity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have been traditionally open and welcoming of diversity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Yes, it will be increasingly difficult to try and balance the competing views and interests.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But let us instead instil, especially in our young, a sense of curiosity and appreciation of diversity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Parents, teachers, professionals, community and religious leaders, and our young must continue to stand together and guard against any threat that seeks to divide us.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have Shahrany Hassan who led a SGfuture session in February to engage youths from all backgrounds in a discussion on topics for social cohesion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We also have a National University of Singapore (NUS) Engineering undergraduate, Muzakkir Samat, who co-edited a book, "From Walden to Woodlands", an inter-faith anthology of poetry about nature in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The book showcases a wide range of writings for anyone interested in faith, nature and the environment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have netizens who speak up with moral clarity against injustice and stereotypes, without anger or judgement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is our duty to not only seek knowledge, read widely and beyond religious texts, Page: 11 but also learn about other cultures, other religions and other societies so that we better appreciate what we have with us.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Taking part in candid but respectful discussions with people of different backgrounds will help us learn about one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We need to be well-read and respectful as we balance differences in ideas, concerns and interests and to gain a consensus to find the best possible solution.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is what we need in our people, and to build on this legacy for our future generations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In 2018, MUIS will be commemorating its 50th anniversary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We want to document this journey on how we have worked together to overcome our challenges and the philosophy and rationale under-girding key policies, so that this will guide future leaders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One area that shows our community's journey in adapting to changes affecting our religious life is the development of our fatwas or religious advice.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One important group is our religious leaders, as pointed out by Mr Zainal Sapari.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our asatizahs play an important role in guiding the community in the values of integrity, respect for human dignity and compassion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have many young and upcoming asatizahs in our community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One example is Ustaz Muslim bin Amad a 25-year-old imam at Al-Muttaqin mosque in Ang Mo Kio.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Apart from discharging his duties diligently as a religious teacher, Ustaz Muslim is a keen advocate of inter-faith work and regularly organises inter-faith initiatives, together with other youth leaders of other faiths.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: He enjoys being involved in inter-faith work and his key message is: "Listen more, talk less.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Be good to all, regardless of race, language or religion".

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To nurture all our asatizahs, we are looking at ways to build up their capabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We also want to ensure that our asatizahs have the confidence of the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will engage the asatizah fraternity to discuss this later this year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have been doing well in these areas and will continue to do better.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Amrin Amin asked about our educational efforts in the coming year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Meanwhile, MENDAKI will continue to resource parents of low-income families with skills to help impart the joy of reading to their kids and parenting toolkits to help their children to be school-ready.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Thirdly, Madam, MENDAKI will improve the learning experience of our MTS students by training our tutors based on a better understanding of the motivational profiles of our students.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is done in conjunction with the National Institute of Education via two research projects.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This was necessary to meet the critical needs of our community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Since 2009, we have built two mosques and upgraded 17, providing more prayer spaces for Muslim congregants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Assoc Prof Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim sought an update on what the community can look forward to.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The increase in prayer spaces will come from the upgrading of five mosques under the Mosque Upgrading Programme Phase 2, the redevelopment of Darul Ghufran Mosque, the completion of the Maarof Mosque in Jurong West later this year, and the Yusof Ishak Mosque in Woodlands in early 2017.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the interim, the prayer space crunch at Al-Istighfar Mosque will be relieved by a temporary covered prayer space opposite the mosque later this year to cater to about 500 congregants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But for the longer term, MUIS will upgrade Al-Istighfar.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Last year, Madam, I shared our long-term plans to build a new mosque in Tampines North.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Over the past year, we have been working with Government agencies to identify a suitable location for the mosque, bearing in mind the needs of the future neighbourhood town.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The mosque will serve residents and workers there and will also be accessible to those staying in Pasir Ris and Punggol.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Madrasah Arabiah is currently sited at the old Poi Ching School in Toa Payoh, on a Temporary Occupation Licence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will start the redevelopment from early next year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: More importantly, Madam, let us focus our minds on providing the best possible education for our kids.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is the point raised by Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar on how we encourage the use of ICT in teaching and learning for our madrasah students.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Madrasah Irsyad Zuhri Al-Islamiah collaborated with the Infocomm Development Authority (IDA) to set up a Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) laboratory to expose madrasah students to Page: 13 game designing and educational robotics programming.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Madrasah Aljunied is piloting the teaching of Arabic Language using iBooks to make learning more interactive.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our preparations to implement the enhanced Joint Madrasah System (JMS) curriculum and syllabi for the secondary level are progressing well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Arabic, Islamic law and theology subjects for Madrasah Aljunied, and the Islamic Studies subject for Madrasah Arabiah will be rolled out.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In tandem, our teachers are being equipped with the skills and resources to implement the curriculum effectively.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We want to help all madrasah students to do the best that they can.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about our efforts to strengthen part-time Islamic education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To meet growing demand for Adult Islamic Learning (ADIL), MUIS has added two more ADIL centres, bringing the number of centres to 15.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MUIS will introduce intermediate modules that focus on the theme of Singaporean Muslims and Contemporary Challenges.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Office of Mufti has also partnered mosques to offer free ADIL modules, and close to 2,400 participants have benefited from ADIL programmes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MUIS will also continue to work with the Private Islamic Education Network to offer quality Islamic education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This includes the Kids aLIVE Home edition that we started last year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For the older youths, the Youth aLIVE classes and seminars discuss issues and challenges relevant to them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will step up efforts against extremist influences online.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The curricula of both aLIVE and ADIL include lessons that help inoculate our youths against online radicalisation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are actively engaging parents on cyber safety for their children so that they are more critical with what they read online.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In so doing, our young are better protected against radical teachings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For the wider community, the Office of Mufti and the Religious Rehabilitation Group are working together to develop both print and online materials to provide guidance in countering extremist ideologies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, I am pleased to inform Mr Zaqy Mohamad that we will enhance the Student Resource Development Secretariat in MUIS into the Student Welfare and Careers Office to better cater to those seeking Islamic religious education overseas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This office will provide education and career guidance, so that the students and their parents can make informed choices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about the support for vulnerable families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are able to help more families because of the generosity of our community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MUIS disburses zakat to an average of 5,300 beneficiaries annually.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Page: 14 To help families on assistance programmes to get back on their feet more quickly, MUIS also runs the Empowerment Partnership Scheme (EPS).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: EPS helps families through services, such as skills upgrading, family management and children's enrichment support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Meanwhile, MENDAKI continues to complement national efforts to offer various programmes and services that equip low-income families with relevant skills, such as Program Bijak Belanja, which teaches financial management skills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MENDAKI also helps families by extending Education Trust Fund subsidies to help their young children access more educational support and, through Family Excellence Circles, provide a safe platform for low-income families to support one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MENDAKI also started the MENDAKI@Heartlands initiative in 2013.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Two centres opened in Woodlands and Pasir Ris.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Together with MUIS, MENDAKI set up four additional centres at the mosques.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These six centres, located islandwide, enable MENDAKI to connect the less advantaged to social assistance offered by the Social Service Offices (SSOs).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Over 400 referrals, including individuals and families, were made to mosques and SSOs for social assistance, while another 600 were matched to educational programmes, job placement and skills upgrading.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Muhammad Faisal Abdul Manap asked about the Malay/Muslim Community Development Fund (MMCDF).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The funding criteria is based on ground-up initiatives that are in line with MENDAKI's mission to support the community in areas, such as education, youth, family and employability.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Developing and delivering programmes in these areas are not core to the objectives of the mosque.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The core objective of the mosque is to facilitate the community's religious life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our mosques, nevertheless, can play a supporting role by providing their premises to MMOs who deliver such programmes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mosques can tap on zakat funds to run programmes for families and the young which are religious in nature or which involve values and character development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, the divorce rate for Muslim couples with younger grooms aged 20 to 24, was 1.5 times higher than those of older grooms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will, hence, provide a stronger focus on strengthening the marriages of young couples in addition to those of minor couples.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: From the second half of this year, our INSPIRASI Hubs will extend their services to couples with grooms aged 21 to 24.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our dedicated counsellors are at the forefront of supporting these couples.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Some couples may also need more guidance to transit to family life while balancing their careers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Over her eight years at the Hub, Mdm Habibah has guided many couples and she goes the extra mile to ensure that those under her care receive the best support in addressing their marital challenges.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Meanwhile, on the query by Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef on the number of Muslim marriages involving minors, this number has been on a steady decline.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These proportions had declined significantly from 3.9% of Muslim grooms and 13.8% of brides in 2004.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked about differentiated approaches to strengthen marriages.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For first marriages, the "Cinta Abadi Marriage of a Lifetime" marriage preparation programme has seen an Page: 15 encouraging increase in participation in 2015.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Later this year, couples in the first 10 years of marriage can benefit from the pilot roll-out of the Cinta Abadi marriage enrichment programme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This programme includes marriage "health checks" and experiential learning, through which couples can build resilience in their marriage, as well as renegotiate their multiple roles, including their roles as parents.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For remarriages and stepfamilies, Persatuan Pemudi Islam Singapura (PPIS) Vista Sakinah offers counselling and therapeutic services to those seeking support for issues related to step family adjustment and child management.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There are also workshops for children to help them adapt to step family life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked about plans to enhance capabilities of our practitioners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The programme will help practitioners understand marriages, divorces and inheritance as practised in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Syariah Court will also be producing the next set of the Singapore Syariah Appeals Reports (SSARs) in the second half of this year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The SSAR provides a source of reference on Muslim family law which is vital to the development and advancement of Islamic jurisprudence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Divorcing couples who have children aged 14 or below are highly encouraged to discuss their post-divorce parenting plans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This includes plans on their children's welfare, with the guidance of a marriage counsellor outside the Court system for a less adversarial discussion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Syariah Court will also work with As-Salaam Family Support Centre, an MSF-appointed Divorce Support Specialist Agency to equip divorced couples with co-parenting skills and to help them in guiding their children on post-divorce issues under the Parenting Parents and Children Together programme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam also asked about reviewing the Syariah Court's Court processes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Syariah Court established a Quality Service Unit in February 2015 to coordinate timely responses to queries and provide a more positive experience for divorcing couples.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Syariah Court has also improved Court processes, such as providing a differentiated case management process for cases that have a high risk of domestic violence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In tandem with the Syariah Court's efforts, we are looking to amend the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will aim to strengthen our Muslim institutions better manage our community's assets and improve existing measures with respect to Muslim marriages and families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: (In Malay):   : Mdm Chair, Budget 2016 aims to further enhance the socio-economic support for our nation's progress and prosperity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our community should seize the opportunities available and upgrade our skills so that we can be prepared for the challenges ahead.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There are two main challenges that we should think about.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Second, the different types of thinking and the diversity present within our community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Although these challenges are complex, I am sure that we can overcome them, just as our Pioneers were able to overcome the tough times over the last 50 years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The key to this is our perseverance and the close cooperation that exists between the Malay/Muslim community and the Government.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Page: 16 One of the challenges in the new economy is the changes brought about by technological advances.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This has forced our industries to restructure and transform to adapt to the global economic climate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This means that continuous skills upgrading will be crucial while ICT will become the catalyst for progress.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our young people have to be aware of this reality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They must be prepared to enter a job market that will increasingly place emphasis on expertise and experience rather than paper qualifications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In order to help the community become aware of this development, the SMCCI and other MMOs must lead the efforts so that more Malay/Muslim workers and companies can bring value-add in their respective fields.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Yayasan MENDAKI, as an important partner to the Government, will complement national efforts in order to bring the Malay/Muslim community closer to the SkillsFuture movement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MENDAKI will launch several new initiatives, including "Future Ready Mentoring" to guide students from the secondary schools, ITEs and polytechnics in choosing their careers, to match the future job landscape.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The CM-Tech@Heartlands programme that will be launched soon, will be brought to the heartlands to generate interest among our young people in the field of technology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The second challenge is managing the diversity in our socio-religious life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Fundamentally, our lives are very much guided by universal values like moderation, inclusivity and respecting differences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This was depicted by our pioneers like President Yusof Ishak, Ustaz Ahmad Sondhaji Mohamed, Pak Ridzwan Dzafir and Ustaz Ibrahim Kassim.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In essence, the Malay/Muslim community made important contributions towards the harmony and wellbeing of Singapore's plural society, in addition to being confident in practising our religious life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The fact is that Malay/Muslims are used to diversity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Even from early on, we are known to be a community that is open and able to accept diversity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I admit that, with challenges becoming even more complex today, it has become increasingly difficult for us to balance all the different interests and views.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Nonetheless, as a mature community, we must continue to instil the value of being able to appreciate diversity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Every group – including parents, teachers, professionals as well as community and religious leaders – must play a part in rejecting elements that can harm our solidarity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This conference will be a platform to discuss and encourage progressive thinking, especially for a minority Muslim community living in a multiracial and multireligious society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Several Members of Parliament have also asked about the efforts to further enhance support towards education, socio-religious needs, family development and assistance to the less fortunate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have achieved much progress in these areas, and a lot more can be achieved in the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are thankful that we are able to establish, and in fact, able to enhance our institutions so that we can fulfil our community's religious needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For the madrasah sector, Madrasah Al-Arabiah will move to a new location with a new 30-year lease.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In line with a technology-based economy, MUIS is also supporting efforts to infuse technology and info-communications in teaching and studying at Madrasah Irsyad Zuhri and Madrasah Aljunied.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Strong families form the backbone of a strong community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Hence, the partnership between the community, MMOs and the Government becomes more critical.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The spirit of giving among our Malay/Muslim community has allowed the zakat collection to increase year after year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Every year, MUIS distributes the zakat to some 5,300 beneficiaries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Yayasan MENDAKI is also working to enhance efforts to refer the needy to social service centres at the national level.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Over the last six years, more than 14,000 individuals have received assistance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In order to further strengthen families, we must focus on efforts to provide our children with the best possible start, especially those who come from low-income families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Hence, Yayasan MENDAKI will work with ECDA so that vulnerable Malay/Muslim families will benefit from the KidSTART initiative.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This initiative will provide support in various aspects, including health, education and the development of children under six years old.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are hopeful that our young people can continue this struggle, by moving forward resolutely, having faith during our journey and taking actions that have been carefully considered.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Clearly, a bright future requires a concerted effort from everyone in the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Let us work together and spark the partnership further between the Malay/Muslim community and the Government in order to create a brighter future for all of us.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As the saying goes, "Good manners are emulated; good people are valued; good citizens are admired." Madam, allow me to conclude in English.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: (In English): Madam, the story of the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore is not about the achievements that we have made over the past 50 years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is about our struggles to find our place in a new nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is about the choices we made that changed the course of our community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is about choosing for ourselves to be a part of this work in progress we call Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: That journey, Madam, has shaped us to become more confident, more assured and, most importantly, more grateful for what life has given us.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We should be proud of what we have achieved.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Indeed, we are in a better position than we were 50 years ago and cannot afford to be reckless or assume we have arrived.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But we must remain humble, for the journey is never over.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Just as our Pioneers struggled to make a nation out of disparate communities, struggle hard we must, as we move into the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, let us not wait for others to find the solutions to the challenges that trouble and pain Page: 18 us.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: That we have so many Singaporeans today stepping forward to right a wrong and create a kinder, more inclusive nation should inspire us to nurture that spirit of doing good among all Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Let us learn to forgive, work together, counsel and support one another and work towards the good of Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As a community, let us help our young to believe that they, too, can make a difference to the lives of others and inspire them in their journey with conviction and moral courage to do what is right for Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Together with our young, let us step forward to take ownership in charting the next chapter of Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: United in partnership within our community and with the rest of Singapore, and with the Government's continued support, we shall overcome whatever challenges may come our way.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our hearts, our hopes, and our dreams are one with our fellow Singaporeans, because Singapore is our home.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The People's Association's (PA's) mission is to strengthen the social fabric of our nation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For an increasingly diverse population and increasingly sophisticated population, the People's Association (PA) has our challenges cut out for us.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Long gone were the days when we just needed to put one black and white television at the basketball court and it would bring out the whole kampung for everyone to bond together.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The range of programmes that PA has to undertake now for an increasingly diverse and sophisticated population is very different from what it used to be in the past.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The second way that we do to strengthen the social fabric of our nation is to make sure that we work with the Ministries to provide timely feedback to the Government of the day on our people's concerns and aspirations, so that the Government of the day can make better policies to serve our people.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The third way that PA seeks to strengthen the social fabric of our nation is to work with our Ministries to explain and execute the policy intent of the government of the day.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This includes explaining the recent Budget measures, explaining and reaching out to our Pioneer Generation about the Pioneer Generation Package, explaining and reaching out to every Singaporean on the MediShield Life plans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, the breadth and depth of PA's work has increased, in tandem with the needs of our country.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked how has the Budget changed for PA.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, on aggregate, the decline for the overall budget is about 5%.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Page: 19 Ms Sylvia Lim asked whether this increase in the last two years is a result of the SG50 celebrations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Most of the SG50 activities ride on existing programmes that have already been planned by the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We started up the office to reach out to all the Pioneer Generation elders, so that we can explain to them, mobilise the volunteers to reach out to them, not only for them to understand the policies but, more importantly, for us to reach out to them to see if they are well taken care of by their families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, that accounts for the bulk of the increase in our Operating Expenditure.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The bigger bulk of the increase is the Capital Expenditure and there are two projects that are parked under the PA's budget which contributed to this significant increase.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: One is the building of Our Tampines Hub.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, is the building of Wisma Geylang Serai Civic Centre.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim might ask, "Is this the correct time to upgrade the Community Clubs?" Yes and no; it all depends.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have a schedule to upgrade our Community Clubs progressively.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Within the margins, we try to find the best time to do it, taking into consideration the following: one, do we have the budget available from the macro national perspective?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Two, are we able to get bang for the buck?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Are we able to stretch those dollars that we spend?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, during the current economic slowdown, if there are opportunities for us to lock in good prices for us to do our routine projects, I think we should do it.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But on the whole, PA adopts a consistent approach to stretch every dollar that we spend.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It does not do us any good to have a feast-and-famine strategy in our capital expenditures.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim, in her remarks yesterday, seems to allege that PA is partisan.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: PA does not check on the political allegiance of the participants of our activities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Nor do I or anyone know their voting preferences.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Personally, I have seen participants of PA activities supporting both the incumbent and the Opposition during the elections.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When I see my own residents, participants of my PA activities supporting the Opposition, I can only ask myself how I can work harder to win them over.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It executes the directions for the Government of the day as per any Statutory Board.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: PA does not allow any political activity or canvassing on our premises or in our activities, and we certainly do not mobilise anyone for any political party.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: If Ms Sylvia Lim has any such evidence of wrongdoing, she can let me know and I guarantee her I will follow up.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I will be the last person to ever allow PA to be politicised.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim talked about working with the Citizens' Consultative Committee (CCC).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I do not have the details of the incident that she raised.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On how the Ministry of National Development works with the Town Council and the CCC to upgrade the various estates, I think Senior Minister of State Mohamad Maliki has already replied to that on record last year.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I have heard from both sides on the ground accusing each other of being uncooperative.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: All I can say is that I urge both sides, be it the Town Council or CCC, to always remember to put the interests of the residents first.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In life, when things get done, there is never a shortage of people Page: 20 who will claim credit.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When things are not done, there is always a shortage of people who will claim responsibility.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is not the way we want to go.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is bad politics and this is not leadership.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, I would urge all parties on the ground to work together to put the interests of the residents first and foremost.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Residents are wise enough to know who have worked hard for them and who have served them well.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And residents will also be wise enough to know who have not worked hard and who have not served them well.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is a work that we all want to embark on and we all want to succeed together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SG50 was a very special year, with many defining moments.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We celebrated and rallied together as one nation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Across the island, we witnessed spontaneous expressions of pride in being Singaporean.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: From a migrant society 50 years ago with no national roots or history, we have become a people capable of cohesive action.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But we cannot take our progress for granted.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As we plan for Singapore's next 50 years, there will be new challenges to overcome and fresh opportunities to seize.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are a small and vulnerable country in a more turbulent world.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In a globalised world, the aftershocks of economic crises, disease and terrorism ripple out to affect all of us.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Information is disseminated instantaneously at an unprecedented scale, yet giving recipients little time for deep reflection.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Technology-enabled social networks have created a new kind of citizen activism.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: All these developments have the potential to either bring us together or pull us apart.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak spoke about the need to rally Singaporeans to co-create our future together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the face of these challenges, our ability to forge a brighter future for all Singaporeans will depend on two things.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If we are confident and proud of who we are as Singaporeans, we will be able to stand fast and resolute in the face of adversity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our sense of who we are is shaped at three levels.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On an individual level, we have our own personal beliefs, experiences and interests.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But we are also members of a community or communities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our ethnicity, religion, politics, interests, schools that we attended, companies that we worked for, give us Page: 21 common identities despite our unique individuality.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They enrich our sense of self and help define our place in society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The challenge of every nation and particularly, for a young multiracial country like Singapore, is how to foster solidarity when society is made up of diverse groups; how to avoid polarisation and exclusivity when groups project their position.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have to embrace a common purpose that is bigger than our differences.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It starts with shared experiences and shared memories.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Every Primary 5 kid participates in the National Day Parade National Education show.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The men would all have gone through National Service.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We know our char kway teow, roti prata and nasi lemak and we can all speak some Singlish.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These things might not seem like much, but they add up to a common way of seeing the world.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When Singaporeans talk to one another, we share a common reference and vocabulary that need no explanation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Being Singaporean is also about sharing the values that our country stands for.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They have been imperative to our success and security.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Justice, equality and progress are not just words, but active ingredients in how our country works.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In all the important spheres of life, such as access to good education, medical care, housing and justice, every citizen stands on equal footing, irrespective of wealth, race or religion.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Every Singaporean can build a better future for their children through hard work and discipline.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Being Singaporean is also about knowing our history and heritage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The story of Singapore is the story of us, where we came from and how we got here.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As a country with no natural resources, Singapore had to be built on the back of human endeavour.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Singapore is a triumph of will and the sacrifices of our parents and grandparents.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Singapore is our home and our children's home.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We all have a part in building the future, by working together, by doing our best and by making the most of the opportunities before us.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We can all lay claim to Singapore's future because it is for us to shape.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If we understand what defines us as Singaporeans, then national pride will grow over time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And there is much to be proud of.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As a country, we made a virtue out of having no resources.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through tenacity and sacrifice, we became a modern, vibrant and dynamic city state.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are also a country that nurtures its own, helps its citizens to realise their potential and gives them the opportunity to do well and excel.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the sporting and cultural fields, Singaporeans are making their mark in the regional and international arena.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are proud of them because they wear our flag on their sleeves and over their hearts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We cheered on our sporting heroes when they represented Team Singapore at the Southeast Asian (SEA) Games and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Para Games and will continue to do so at the Olympics and Paralympics later this year.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many of us follow closely the artistic achievements of our artists, musicians and film directors and appreciate what they tell us about Singapore society and character.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We feel a sense of pride when we look up to our sporting and cultural heroes, not just because of the awards and accolades Page: 22 they win, but also because they represent the best of the human spirit and exemplify the values that we aspire to as Singaporeans – hard work, determination, passion, teamwork.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They make us proud of who we are as a people.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We feel that no one should be left to struggle on their own because we are all in this together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We want to look out for one another because we know we are only as strong as the most vulnerable among us.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This came out strongly during Our Singapore Conversation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: During the Budget debate, Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin spoke about how we need to overcome a mindset based on scarcity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Such a mindset reduces everything to a zero-sum game.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It causes people to think that others gain at their expense.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think the best way to overcome this is by cultivating a sense of empathy and care.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This means recognising the worth and dignity of our fellowmen, that we are part of one another's lives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When we care, it might be helping only one person or improving just a corner of our neighbourhood.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They make a difference, not just for the beneficiary, but for the giver.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That is how we discover our strengths and weaknesses and the depths of our compassion.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That is how we grow as individuals and grow closer to the ones we serve.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We start to measure success not by how far we are ahead of the next person, but by how many of our fellow Singaporeans we bring along.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are not just bystanders, but invest ourselves, our energy and our purpose to make Singapore a better place.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In this way, when we feel responsible for one another, we also erase the lines that divide us.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Service binds us to our fellow citizens, to our communities and to our country.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is the social glue that makes us a cohesive society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Arts, Heritage and Sports play an important role in nourishing national identity and pride.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Sports is a great way to rally the nation and has the potential to build national pride.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many Members have spoken about how Singaporeans rallied behind our athletes every step of the way at the SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng will elaborate further on sports excellence.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But I would like to emphasise that sports excellence means far more when Team Singapore athletes give back to the community.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Take para swimmer Yip Pin Xiu, for example.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Pin Xiu is a role model for all of us, not just for overcoming formidable odds to break the world record in the 50-metre backstroke S2 event, but also for taking the time to reach out and inspire others.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: During the Budget debate, Mr Kok Heng Leun said that our literature, music, painting and theatre remind us we are living in one place.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I also agree with him on "the importance of having arts around us and be part of us", and thank him for acknowledging the Government's effort in developing the arts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Local arts and culture are important touchstones for what it means to be Singaporean.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In a very visceral way, through what we see, touch and hear, the arts hold up a mirror that shows us who we are.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The numbers do not tell the whole story.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: An increasing number of seed grant recipients have graduated into the major grant programmes, potentially providing them a longer runway for development.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have also committed more funding to enable our artists to perform on the international stage and further cultural diplomacy.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Page: 24 Later, Parliamentary Secretary Baey will also speak specifically about how we are developing the traditional arts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our funding has enlarged the space for our artists and arts groups to create more original Singapore works across music, visual, performing and literary arts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These works reflect our Southeast Asian context, our multicultural diversity and our Singaporean identity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, in December last year, the Singapore Chinese Orchestra (SCO) staged "Titian Budaya Night: Crossing Cultures in Malaysia", which commemorated 50 years of bilateral relations between Singapore and Malaysia.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Playing to a full house, the multicultural event saw SCO artfully weaving traditional Chinese, Malay and Indian music with Singaporean jazz and even wayang kulit.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the field of literature, NAC commissioned "Singathology: 50 New Works" from Singapore's award-winning writers.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the performing arts, the Singapore International Festival of the Arts commissioned several new Singapore works, including the dance production "Returning", which drew from Chinese, Malay and Indian dance traditions and involved different generations of dance-makers.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Young Singaporeans growing up learning about our rich local cultural scene.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our students know their Shakespeare, but they also read playwrights like Haresh Sharma and Jean Tay who have been part of our GCE "O" level English literature texts, along with collections like "Here and Beyond: 12 Stories" that is commissioned by the Ministry of Education (MOE), supported by NAC.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This includes stories by Singapore writers, like Claire Tham, Simon Tay and Suchen Christine Lim.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The NAC Arts Education programme exposes our students to our leading artists, like award-winning film maker Royston Tan and Cultural Medallion recipients Mdm Som Said for Malay Dance and Jeremy Monteiro, a jazz musician.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Students also attend performances by groups like the Singapore Symphony Orchestra (SSO) and SCO.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When we read these stories, listen to the music, watch the dances, we know they are our own.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Chingay is another good example of how culture reflects and enriches our sense of identity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Every country has its own festival processions, but Chingay is one that is uniquely Singaporean.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Here, you can see that the religious leaders on the top of the float, singing "一人一半", which translates loosely into "sharing is a virtue".

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I was there and was totally impressed by the fact that religious leaders could get together and sing in their respective vernacular languages.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, from the first street parade in 1973, Chingay has evolved from a festivity of the Chinese community to a truly multiracial celebration with performers from diverse backgrounds.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think the important thing here is that the performers themselves are diverse.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In some other contexts, we could see multicultural items, but performed by a single group.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Here, we are seeing performers of different backgrounds coming together for each and every one of the items.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, the performers are foreign and local, young and old, from different races and, by definition, probably have different religions as well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It opens a window into the different cultures of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It represents a country where race, language and creed do not divide, but instead drive a dynamic, multicultural society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members talked about the relationship between people and places and the role public spaces have in building a sense of community.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked what we can learn from other cities Page: 25 to make our works more accessible and pleasurable for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A strong sense of place and local artistic content feature prominently in culturally vibrant places.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will be doing more to enliven the Civic District and Bras Basah-Bugis precinct and deepen the distinctive character of places which make Singapore attractive and unique.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: NAC and the National Heritage Board (NHB) will work with different stakeholders in the community, including arts and heritage groups, to create places that people want to visit and where they can enjoy outdoor and indoor experiences across sports, culture, food and entertainment.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have also started to bring art to local communities and engage them in arts activities that reflect their local identity, through initiatives, like PAssionArts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Parliamentary Secretary Baey will share more about these efforts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Chen Show Mao asked about Heritage Impact Assessment (HIA).

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our shared heritage is an important marker of national identity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But at the same time, identity is not a fixed thing.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There must be space for Singapore to evolve with new developments that meet the needs of future generations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: NHB adopts a calibrated and sensitive approach, involving relevant stakeholders, to balance heritage preservation and development needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There are inevitable trade-offs and differing stakeholder demands in this process.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To guide its HIA efforts, NHB has the Heritage Advisory Panel, which includes experts, academics and industry practitioners.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The panel evaluates the significance of sites, buildings and structures and advises on mitigation measures if they are affected by development works.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We agree with Mr Chen Show Mao's point to have closer coordination with Government agencies.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: NHB works with planning agencies, such as the Urban Redevelopment Authority, Land Transport Authority and Housing and Development Board, to incorporate heritage considerations into long-term and nearer-term land use and development plans.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When the survey is completed in mid-2017, we will have a comprehensive database that maps out Singapore's heritage assets.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: NHB will be able to identify Singapore's heritage assets and better advise on their historical significance to facilitate better decision-making by planning agencies.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang spoke about allowing different interpretations of Singapore history and setting up an independent commission to oversee NHB grants.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: NHB already taps on the expertise of independent external panels to evaluate its grants.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The panels comprise representatives from different sectors, including academics and civic society groups, such as the Singapore Heritage Society, to ensure a wide range of opinions and views.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As NHB does not dictate content, we have seen many different topics and perspectives represented.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: NHB also draws widely on local and international experts in curating exhibitions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: NHB has consulted such experts on the revamp of our Heritage Institutions and the Singapore history galleries at the National Museum of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In particular, on Singapore history, the National Museum is advised by senior historians from our universities who are acknowledged in their fields.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The same applies to the recent exhibition at the Old Parliament House, which Mr Low Thia Khiang mentioned.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Besides Pioneer leaders, various groups, such as opposition party members, minority members and women members are also featured in the visuals and texts of the exhibition.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, Mr Chiam See Tong's quote capturing his perspective on being an opposition party Member of Parliament (MP) is prominently highlighted.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As in other exhibitions, NHB and the Arts House would welcome views and additional information which can further enrich our understanding of history.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Overall, NHB's approach is an open and consultative one.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It takes an objective approach in its curation of history and invites visitors to examine different perspectives and engage in critical thinking, rather than impose a "standard" or "official" account of history, as Mr Low Thia Khiang says.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This series of radio talks aimed to expose the goals, methods and organisation of the Communist movement.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But the showcase also presents two alternative political perspectives published at the time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the booklet, she urged the people to question the People's Action Party's (PAP's) campaign for merger and make an informed decision when casting their votes during the referendum.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The above example illustrates how NHB seeks to present curatorial viewpoints based on facts and comprehensive research from multiple available sources.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At the same time, NHB welcomes new sources of information and viewpoints that enrich our understanding of our past through different perspectives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The fabric of a society is delicately woven, strand by strand, from the small daily interactions we have with our neighbours, friends and family.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Page: 27 Research tells us that the experiences we share and the everyday exchanges we have are the building blocks of social cohesion.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is why we see public spaces like our museums, galleries, sports facilities as important common spaces where everyone of us from different walks of life can meet one another, experience the same things together and build trust, consideration and understanding on a daily basis.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our museums and galleries have a special place in the hearts and minds of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The National Gallery alone saw almost 700,000 go through its doors since it opened late last year.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will ensure our collections and facilities are meaningful to Singaporeans from all walks of life, through programming and place-making.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will design our programmes to enable everyone to participate, whether young or old, rich or poor, able-bodied or not.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: During the Budget debate, Mr Kok Heng Leun spoke about the lack of space for discourse and for art to ask difficult questions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: He also quoted Lu Xun to explain that the nature of art is to examine change, to pursue truth.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: However, as the nature of politics is to maintain the status quo, according to Lu Xun, art and politics will diverge.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
