text: Politics in Singapore does not seek to maintain the status quo.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we have made changes and adjustments along the way.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Norms of what are acceptable or not, evolve.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Compared to a generation ago, there is more space for expression and experimentation, while still preserving peaceful social relations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But there is, ultimately, a need for rules of engagement to safeguard the social harmony that we cherish, which then creates the safe space for citizens to pursue their aspirations and for art to do its work.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To quote Henry Kissinger: "Any system of world order, to be sustainable, must be accepted as just – not only by leaders but also by citizens.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It must reflect two truths: order without freedom, even if sustained by momentary exaltation, eventually creates its own counterpoise; yet freedom cannot be secured or sustained without a framework of order to keep the peace.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Order and freedom, sometimes described as opposite poles on the spectrum of experience, should instead be understood as interdependent." While Kissinger wrote these words in the context of world order, I think it appropriately describes the Singapore context as well, a recognition that the Government has to balance order and freedom; and that our role is to drive progress while remaining in step with the populace and maintaining societal order.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is only with social harmony that we can enjoy the peace and, ultimately, the freedom that comes with it.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Sport is a great way to bring diverse communities together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: ActiveSG, which was launched two years ago as our national movement for sport, contributes to this.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: ActiveSG has over a million members now and offers a wide range of programmes catering to different ages and interests.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked about sustaining sports participation across life stages.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: ActiveSG will launch sports academies and clubs across Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The academies will offer structured programmes in selected sports for youths to develop their skills.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The clubs will organise events to enable all Singaporeans to enjoy sports.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They will host interest groups, community and corporate leagues with varying levels of competitiveness for participants of all ages and skill levels to stay active and grow their social networks through sports.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, perhaps, we should revive our MP Page: 28 Football Club and participate in one of these corporate leagues.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These leagues and community clubs will complement and supplement the schools and address concerns, such as inability to get into a school team, and provide opportunities to play even when a sport is not covered by a particular school.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A caring society is one enriched by service and responsibility to one another.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is a society where we give back our time, talent and treasure freely.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It involves active citizenship, which matters because, in a more turbulent future, the challenges we face will require action that exceeds the limits of the Government.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Government will build strong partnerships with the people, the theme of this Budget.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For many years, the Government has consulted citizens on policies and to gather feedback.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Ministries conduct surveys and consult stakeholders in our policy-making process.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To build a common future together, MCCY will create more avenues for citizens to step forward, lend a hand and be part of the solutions to the problems we face.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The public can contribute by giving views on policies, organising local activities or volunteering a service to the needy.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members Ms Joan Pereira, Dr Lily Neo, Mr Melvin Yong spoke on the importance of volunteerism.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SG50 saw many examples of Singaporeans contributing time and effort to various causes, offering help during the mourning period for the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew, volunteering for Team Nila during the SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games and donating generously to Care&Share@SG50.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We want to grow this culture of caring and giving.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MCCY will encourage more citizen participation and create more volunteering opportunities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It teaches under-privileged youth how to swim first and then, when they can swim, they will go on to sailing and windsurfing.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: You can see the results of their good work at Jurong West Swimming Complex, where the first batch of youngsters began learning to swim in February.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is volunteerism at its best and we want to enable more of such efforts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We see companies as key partners in growing a culture of giving.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Working adults often do not have time to organise something on their own.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, companies play an important role in creating the opportunities for employees to volunteer for a worthy cause.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Corporate giving also builds relationships between businesses and the communities they serve.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For the employees and beneficiaries involved, corporate social responsibility (CSR) or volunteerism projects are opportunities to make new friends beyond their usual circles.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is a natural setting for employees from different nationalities and ethnicities to get to know one another better.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Thomas Chua, Mr Henry Kwek and Ms Joan Pereira spoke on encouraging corporate giving.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will share more about our efforts to support corporates' CSR efforts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For citizens with good ideas on making Singapore a better home, we will support them with resources to realise their ideas.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Page: 29 Through Our Singapore Fund, MCCY will encourage citizens to take ownership of the future of Singapore and keep the momentum of SG50 going.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked what lessons we have learnt from the SG50 Celebration Fund.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: From the many meaningful projects that surfaced during SG50 that brought our community together, we know there is a rich store of enthusiasm and public spirit.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We want to unlock it with a little support to translate these ideas into reality.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I do not think you could miss them in their purple shirts during SEA Games and the ASEAN Para Games.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These volunteers were deployed in a wide spectrum of roles from ushers, anti-doping officers to safety officers.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They are not athletes and do not compete in the Games, but Team Nila allowed them to participate fully in the Games.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It was a movement and an inclusive community.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Volunteers with disabilities worked alongside those without; volunteers in their teens alongside those in their 70s; children alongside their parents; expatriates alongside locals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Team Nila was a mirror of Singapore's diversity, coming together as one to make the SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games successful.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Rain or shine, our volunteers turned up in full force.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When Maximillian Tan, a para equestrian athlete, found out that his event was not staged in the ASEAN Para Games, he volunteered himself with Team Nila.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Together with his father, he helped train our volunteers in disability etiquette.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Doreen Cady cancelled her holiday plan and went out of her way to take care of the Myanmar delegation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Budi, a new citizen, volunteered with Team Nila multiple times and proudly hosted our Indonesian guests at the Games.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Some volunteer leaders like Ms Dawn Lim went the extra mile to cover shifts for fellow volunteers who had to call in sick.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: She even treated her volunteer group to a barbecue to thank everyone for their work.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The volunteers whom I have met personally were unanimously motivated to leave a good impression with the foreign guests and do Singapore proud.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our foreign guests were able to feel the dedication and sincerity in them and were full of praise for our volunteers.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Team Nila made the SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games much more than events for winning medals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They made them a precious opportunity for volunteerism and the building of social bonds and national identity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Creating platforms for Team Nila and growing the group of volunteers not just in sports but also in the arts, heritage and the community are important tasks for my colleagues.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Next, the Outward Bound School (OBS) @ Coney.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members Ms Denise Phua and Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar spoke in favour of outdoor adventure education, and Mr Darryl David, Ms Sun Xueling, Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about our plans for the OBS Campus on Coney Island.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For any individual, the OBS experience can be transformational.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: During the Budget debate, Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin spoke about the need to overcome the habit of fear.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Darryl David spoke as a loving father about how his young son overcame fear and gained confidence through outdoor adventure learning.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Indeed, the physical challenges at OBS make you confront your fears and overcome them.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When before, fear was a limiting factor, by the time you complete the course, having conquered your fears, you realise there are endless new possibilities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: You are ready for the fears that life might throw at you.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Whether it is the inverse tower or kayak expedition, our youths will be presented with obstacles, challenges and unfamiliar situations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They will learn to work with one another.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They will venture out of their comfort zone.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They will have a chance to experiment, fail and learn from that failure.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As Seow Bei Yi noted in her recent article in Page: 30 The Straits Times, students are allowed to push their limits, fail and recover from it.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: She said, and I quote, "If the OBS experience has taught me anything, it is to face fears head-on, or at least try." Beyond individual development, OBS @ Coney will enable all youths from all backgrounds to benefit from a common OBS experience.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Unlike today, when the majority who go through OBS go with their classmates, we will mix students from different schools.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They will make new friends and journey together throughout the five-day OBS camp.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We hope this experience will form lifelong bonds for many.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As we proceed on this project, Parliamentary Secretary Baey will take the lead in engaging our stakeholders and the public.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin asked how we were helping youths to find their place in the future economy.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: OBS @ Coney is one of many efforts to prepare our youths for the future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: OBS will inspire a sense of adventure, resilience and teamwork in our youths.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These are the skill sets that they will need later on in life.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Committee on the Future Economy is engaging Singaporeans, including young Singaporeans, whose views will factor into the bespoke plans for the economic sectors that the Government is developing.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MOE is shifting away from a prior emphasis on grades to lifelong learning and skills which will prepare our children and youths for the future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In our polytechnics and ITEs, education and career guidance will be structured into the curriculum and developed through industry immersion programmes, talks and workshops.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Student internships will be enhanced to provide more time for on-the-job learning to cover key skills critical to the job, as well as structured mentoring.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin also suggested having bespoke plans for youths.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The National Youth Council (NYC) today offers a plethora of programmes that engage and develop youths of diverse backgrounds and aspirations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, Youth Corps Singapore provides youths with opportunities to be developed as community service leaders.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: OBS also offers a flagship 21-day programme to develop leaders through outdoor adventure.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many young Singaporeans can pursue their aspirations through *SCAPE, music, media, dance and personal development programmes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Last year, the *SCAPE media hub was launched to provide creative space for young media enthusiasts who lack space to work on projects after they leave school.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At the same time, NYC continues to encourage and support ground-up initiatives through our National Youth Fund.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We want to better support youths as they transit from schools to work.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MCCY will coordinate efforts across the Government to engage youths on their need and aspirations at their different life stages.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We embarked on SGfuture in November last year.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Page: 31 SGfuture asks Singaporeans to share their ideas on building a better future for Singapore and act on their projects to help realise this future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It explores with Singaporeans how we can foster a caring community, build a sustainable home, create opportunities for learning and strengthen community and national resilience.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many ground-up projects have surfaced during these engagements.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Intergenerational activities are incorporated to promote education and health issues among the active agers and the young children.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Cheryl did her own research to develop an intergenerational curriculum and shared her ideas at a recent Ministry of Health (MOH) SGfuture dialogue session in February.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And we are seeing Singaporeans coming forward to partner the Government to build a better home together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These are exciting new developments and mark a new approach to governance.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through SGfuture, we are defining our future together and how every Singaporean can play a part in realising it.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The series of SGfuture engagements represents a major step towards promoting citizen engagement across all of Government.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We hope it will jumpstart the building of the whole-of-Government capacity in citizen engagement, extending and expanding citizen engagement efforts in the years to come.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There will be areas of disagreement and issues of complexity that are not easy to navigate.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But we can overcome them in the spirit of partnership.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It has to be an ongoing interaction to build durable partnerships among the people, private and public sectors.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This will require new skills on the part of the Public Service and taking some risks.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But by working together, we can build an even better Singapore in the next 50 years.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the end, every one of us is going to have to share the future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The question is what kind of future and whether we can create a future of shared responsibility and shared prosperity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The road ahead will not be without challenges.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But we can achieve our common vision of a harmonious society, a caring people and a confident nation if every individual, family and community play their part together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: My Ministry will partner Singaporeans to build a stronger Singapore and a better home for all of us.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In this way, we will secure the best future for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Page: 32 Racial and religious harmony is a fundamental value of our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the national level, the National Steering Committee (NSC) on Racial and Religious Harmony is a platform for apex leaders of the major ethnic and religious groups to engage each other and with the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the local level, MCCY supports the activities of Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles (IRCCs), which comprises representatives from ethnic and religious organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They also train community leaders to respond to crises in order to ensure that our communities are resilient to incidents with religious and racial overtones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I agree with Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin that our harmony depends on Singaporeans having respect for one another's beliefs as well as a sense of shared responsibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And it is important that these values are passed down to our youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, I thank Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin, as well as Ms Rahayu Mahzam, for their thoughtful comments on the need to engender open conversations among our youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is necessary if we are to develop a deeper understanding of the need for common spaces, give-and-take and a rich appreciation of one another's beliefs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Schools are natural places to develop our students' sensitivity to different beliefs and practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) and Social Studies, students discuss the need for mutual respect, common space and the consequences of perpetuating stereotypes and prejudices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Beyond the classroom, MCCY supports additional programmes that bring youths together to make friends from different cultures and backgrounds, share common experiences and appreciate one another's beliefs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Conference, which reaches out to some 700 youths each year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This provides a safe space for our youths to converse honestly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, some participants share their personal experiences of racism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Volunteer facilitators lead small-group discussions about the challenges faced by our increasingly diverse society and the personal steps we can take to address them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We want more groups to help make such conversations possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Almost half of these are targeted at youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NYC is also working with IRCCs and various religious and ethnic groups to launch more platforms where youths can have candid and constructive exchanges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I also share Mr Alex Yam's concern that our young may be exposed to online disinformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Yaacob Ibrahim earlier highlighted initiatives undertaken by the Malay/Muslim community against radicalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More generally, parents play a key role in shaping their children's Internet exposure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MOE and the Media Literacy Council have developed cyber wellness resources to help Page: 33 parents guide their children's digital media consumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MOE's cyber wellness curriculum in schools also reinforces positive values so that our students can navigate cyberspace safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   As a multiracial and multi-religious society, Singapore has always viewed racial and religious harmony as one of the fundamental tenets in nation-building.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many places in the world still see conflicts along racial and religious lines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Extremist and violent messages have also become easily broadcast due to the widespread use of the Internet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In this environment, it is difficult to maintain peace and unity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One can even say that it is like swimming against the tide and you will be swept away if you do not keep up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To maintain Singapore's racial and religious harmony, the Government has set up several initiatives and platforms to strengthen mutual understanding, trust and resilience among community groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These include CEP in 2006; NSC, which includes the apex leaders of ethnic and religious groups; and IRCCs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This has resulted in a strong and deeply-rooted network of community groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY, through the Harmony Fund and NYC, also supports activities like dialogues and learning camps that enhance our youths' appreciation and support of racial and religious harmony.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In English): Let me now elaborate on how we will grow our giving culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY works with partners like the National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre (NVPC) to encourage Singaporeans to give.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I agree with Dr Lily Neo that we must find more ways to recognise and support our volunteers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will consider her suggestions as we and our partners refine these programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Grace Fu spoke earlier about how we are supporting ground-up initiatives through Our Singapore Fund and how we will support youth volunteers through the Youth Corps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Joan Pereira wanted to know more about how we are supporting our senior volunteers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As part of the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, we want to create opportunities for seniors to be enriched with productive and meaningful lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It will support the establishment of volunteer management systems, volunteer training and programmes that offer volunteering opportunities to seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another key group of volunteers is our working adults.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We regularly speak of corporate transformation in terms of productivity and innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is just as important that businesses in our future economy are civic-minded and play active roles in our communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ten years ago, it set up its CapitaLand Hope Foundation to donate a portion of its annual profits to support underprivileged children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, CapitaLand staff are given three days of Volunteer Service Leave each year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And when a staff member takes all three days, CapitaLand donates $500 to a charity of their choice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And it is not just large companies that benefit from corporate giving programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: GreenPac is a small and medium enterprise which provides well-designed and environmentally-friendly packaging solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: GreenPac's founder and chief executive officer, Ms Susan Chong, believes in doing well by doing good and she has built this belief into her company's Page: 34 structure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: GreenPac sets itself key performance indicators (KPIs) for giving and appraises its employees on how they give.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The company has donated hydroponic systems to schools and estates in the Jurong neighbourhood, and its staff regularly visit to train students and residents to care for the plants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Having made corporate giving a part of its core principles, GreenPac's employees consistently report workplace satisfaction levels above 90%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will do more to encourage businesses to be more civic-minded, meet the aspirations of their employees and be enterprises of which Singaporeans can be proud.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In his Budget speech, the Minister for Finance spoke about the Business and Institutions of Public Character (IPC) Partnership Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development, in his Committee of Supply speech, spoke about how he is enhancing the ComChest SHARE programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The programme is open to all businesses in Singapore and will empower them to give better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The programme will offer customised levels of support to meet the different needs of businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: All participating businesses will have access to advice, resources and networks where they can share and learn best practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As Mr Thomas Chua suggested, this will help them improve their giving practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Participating businesses can also choose to display a Company of Good logo on their materials.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NVPC will give more details on the Company of Good programme in May.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked about how we can use sports, arts and heritage to encourage more Singaporeans to volunteer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Grace Fu spoke of the commitment of Singaporeans who volunteered during the SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These include sports photography, sports safety and leadership functions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SportSG will also enhance the Sports Volunteer Framework to better engage and recognise volunteers and expand volunteering opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SportSG will also expand its SportCares volunteer movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the arts, the National Arts Council (NAC) has a programme called ArtReach to raise the capability of artists, voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) and rehabilitation centres to use the arts to achieve social outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, NAC partners the Agency for Integrated Care to incorporate the arts into the community care framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Today, one-fifth of our Community Care organisations run arts programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last month, NHB also launched a volunteer programme for the heritage sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HeritageCares will have programmes at NHB museums and other heritage institutions to bond families and communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It will also offer volunteer programmes for the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Foreign charitable purpose trusts are set up by foreigners with foreign sources of funds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They are granted tax exemptions to encourage them to locate their trust Page: 35 management and administration activities in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To get this exemption, they must administer their trust through a Singapore-licensed trust company.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Local charitable purpose trusts, whose sources of funds are local and which advance charitable purposes substantially in Singapore, must register for charity status under the Charities Act in order to enjoy tax exemption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is to safeguard the interest of donors and recipients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To promote charitable giving, we have made our regulations for these trusts easy to comply with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Under the lighter-touch regulatory regime, qualifying grant-makers, including local charitable trusts that do not solicit funds from the public, only need to comply with the basic requirements of filing annual reports and financial accounts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, they have a significantly lower regulatory burden than other charities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will study the point raised by Ms Foo and review with partner agencies if necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I will now address Mr Alex Yam's query about how we are making our arts and heritage spaces more accessible to those with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NHB will continue to consult on how it can further improve the visitor experience for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked about how we can help more people with disabilities benefit from sports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last year, MCCY set up the Committee for Disability Sports and MCCY has accepted the recommendations proposed by the Committee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There are three thrusts under the Disability Sports Master Plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SportSG will also work with MOE to develop relevant sports programmes for schools with students with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we will develop the necessary organisational and professional capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SportSG and the Singapore Disability Sports Council will work with sports associations and healthcare institutions to introduce sports for rehabilitation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, we will build awareness of disability sports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SportSG will work with NVPC to develop a support network for disability sports through volunteerism and corporate philanthropy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will also continue to showcase our inspirational para-athletes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY will continue to work with our people to make Singapore an inclusive society with a culture of contribution.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: At last year's SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games, we saw the power of sports in bringing together Singaporeans from all walks of life, as we celebrated our athletes' achievements as One Team Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue to build a stronger community and inspire the Singapore spirit through sports.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked how we will continue to provide quality opportunities so that we can make sports a lifestyle for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Working adults currently make up more than half of the membership.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Almost two-thirds of members have started to utilise their $100 ActiveSG credits.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Going beyond facilities, we continued to offer innovative programmes at our sports centres, such as Piloxing, which is a fusion of pilates, boxing and dance, or Stand Up Paddling, a mix of canoeing and surfing.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It is heartening to see so many Singaporeans onboard ActiveSG, but what is more important is for members to continue participating in sports, even as they transit across different life stages.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: That is why we are stepping up efforts for sports to score four "As" − Available, Accessible, Anytime, Anywhere.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will expand ActiveSG programmes and grow the sporting capabilities in a number of sports domains to encourage broad-based participation and for people to stay engaged in the sport.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Through the ActiveSG Sports Academies and Clubs, there will be a variety of opportunities and structured programmes for Singaporeans to keep an active lifestyle.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example, we recently launched the ActiveSG Football Academy under the leadership of former national player Aleksandar Duric.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Academy will benefit many youths, including nine-year-old Ong Kai Le from Canberra Primary School, who was not selected for his school's football team, but has a strong passion for football.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Through the Academy, he will now have more opportunities not only to play football, but also to learn and improve in the sport.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In the upcoming months, we will roll out Basketball and Tennis Academies as well as Athletics Club, giving more opportunities for the public to pick up a new sport, develop both sporting and life skills, and possibly go on to pursue the sport competitively.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Besides providing events and programmes for members, we also want to enhance the gotong-royong spirit through the ActiveSG movement, by allowing members and community partners to take on more active roles in designing and implementing programmes at our sports centres.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: To rejuvenate our shared sporting spaces, we partnered the students of Fernvale Primary School to liven up the walls of Sengkang Sports Centre with their murals, and we hope to expand this to other sports centres as well.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked about improving our sporting facilities, which we aim to achieve under the Sports Facilities Master Plan (SFMP).

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As Members are aware, we are continuing to work on several major projects in Bedok, Punggol, Sembawang and Tampines as part of SFMP.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Due to the phasing of public sector infrastructure projects at the national level to manage constraints, such as construction manpower, upcoming developments in the pipeline will have to be phased out Page: 37 over the longer term, probably after 2020.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In the interim, we will continue to step up programming efforts under ActiveSG in Yishun, as well as other areas.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example, at Yishun Sports Centre, as part of the popular ActiveSG School Holiday Sports Programmes, we recently conducted camps for basketball and flippa ball, which is modified water polo in shallow pools.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We have also conducted mini-tennis programmes in schools, including Naval Base Primary School in Nee Soon South.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: With the launch of the ActiveSG Tennis Academy later this year, mini-tennis programmes will also be offered to the wider public at our sports centres and indoor sports halls under the Dual-Use Scheme in Yishun as well as other areas.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We aim to open up all the remaining indoor sports halls and fenced fields in Government primary and secondary schools under the Dual-Use Scheme by around 2020.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As we provide sporting opportunities and spaces for all Singaporeans, we remain committed to sports excellence.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Members like Mr Ganesh Rajaram, Mr Darryl David and Mr Alex Yam highlighted the importance of supporting our athletes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: At the recent SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games, our spexScholars contributed about one-third of Team Singapore's medal haul.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Several of them have also qualified for Rio 2016.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Other carded athletes receive training allowances, coaching and sports medicine and sports science services under the various spexSchemes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Team Singapore athletes who have qualified or are on track to qualify for the Games are supported under the spexScholarship and Race to Rio programmes, where they are provided with enhanced support that they need to prepare for the Games.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Even as they excel on the international stage, many of our athletes, like Yip Pin Xiu, give back to the wider community.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Ex-national footballers have joined ActiveSG Football Academy as Sport Ambassadors to groom the next generation of football lovers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our national badminton players conduct clinics for aspiring shuttlers at our sports centres.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Micky Lin, our national netball team captain, shared with young Singaporeans at a recent forum about her life growing up and how she managed to balance studies with her sporting pursuits.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Beyond excelling in the field, our athletes are developing a following, spreading a sporting culture and making a positive difference to the lives of other Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I agree with Mr Ganesh Rajaram that it takes a village to raise a champion.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In fact, I am very heartened by Mr and Mrs Ganesh's unwavering support for their son's aspiration to pursue a professional career in football.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: He told me that his son has already represented his football club in the Under-16 World Club Championships in Sweden last July.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We hope to hear more of such stories and we need to work with parents, schools and corporates to build an environment conducive to the pursuit of sports excellence from young.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: That Page: 38 is why we have the Sports School, the spexEducation Scheme and the spexBusiness Network to help athletes cope with the demands of studies or career through flexible academic and work arrangements.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Building on the success of the Singapore Sports School (SSP), we recently set up the National Youth Sports Institute (NYSI) to support our youth athletes in their pursuit of sporting excellence.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This dedicated support for youth training and development will extend beyond SSP to other mainstream schools, starting with selected sports.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It will do so by working with National Sports Associations (NSAs) to develop their systems for youth coaching and youth athlete development as well as long-term development plans for promising youth athletes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Alex Yam will be happy to note that table tennis is one of the nine identified sports, and NYSI is working closely with the Singapore Table Tennis Association to provide targeted sports science support for national youth team paddlers from SSP as well as from other mainstream schools.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In time, NYSI's partnership with NSAs could expand beyond these nine sports.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In addition, the institute has started working with various partners including MOE, the Singapore Sport Institute (SSI) and NSAs to build more pathways for sporting talents to emerge and to provide more opportunities for these junior athletes to grow and develop their potential in sports and, more importantly, in life.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Alex Yam asked how NYSI will complement the existing SSI which is under SportSG.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NYSI is aimed at supporting our high-performing student athletes from age 12 to 18, while SSI supports older elite athletes who are competing at the senior level.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The training design, strength and conditioning programme and recovery for young adolescent athlete are quite different from an adult athlete.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For instance, when do you start with weight training?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These are important questions which our team of specialists can now provide answers to.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Nonetheless, NYSI and SSI will work closely together to strengthen the national athlete pipeline and build a seamless progression pathway for current and future generations of sportsmen and sportswomen.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We hope to show through these programmes that more talented athletes will pursue their dreams of representing Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We hope that, over time, mindsets will change and more Page: 39 parents will support their children's aspirations to go into sports and more schools are willing to exercise greater flexibility for student athletes to pursue their sporting goals.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, quoting Mr Ganesh, "Let's be sporting about our children's choice in sports".

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin spoke about promoting community arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our community arts programmes and initiatives have been specially designed to make the arts more accessible to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Arts in your Neighbourhood series reached out to almost 90,000 attendees in 2015.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This year, we will be making the series more attractive with interactive projects that the community can participate in.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we welcome Dr Teo Ho Pin to offer Bukit Panjang Art Street to play host to future editions of Arts in our Neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will also continue to develop more Arts and Culture Community Nodes to dedicate more community spaces for the arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Through the PAssionArts programme and the annual PAssionArts Festival, we have been boosting exposure, interest and participation in community arts by residents and grassroots enthusiasts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This adds buzz and builds attachment to community spaces.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: A great example of this is the beautifully painted Kolam Ayer Bridge.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Named "Rainbow", this work of art was designed by local Visual Artist Shah Rizzal and painted by more than 200 residents of Kolam Ayer.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Under the PAssionArts Hotspots programme, residents can also showcase their other artworks right in the heart of the neighbourhood, in spaces like hawker centres, parks and playgrounds.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: By partnering citizens to co-create artworks, we can involve residents who are new to art, enliven conventional community spaces and bring these enriching experiences closer to home.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In fact, last year's PAssionArts partnered the Singapore International Festival of Arts (SIFA) to bring the arts experience into the homes of residents in the heartlands.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Artist-mentors were engaged to work with 25 homeowners to transform their living rooms into theatres.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, even ordinary Singaporeans had the opportunity to work with artist-mentors to co-create art works for a prominent festival like SIFA.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As Mr Kok Heng Leun highlighted, the Arts and Culture Strategic Review has seen significant investment to increase the accessibility of community arts and we agree that efforts to promote community arts should go beyond one-off projects to bring opportunities to experience and participate in art-making to the community.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It should look at how the arts can be made a more integral part of our lives.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: That is why initiatives like PAssionArts and the Arts in your Neighbourhood series are ongoing efforts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue to broaden access and the reach of the arts and enhance the quality and diversity of programmes to deepen engagement within the community.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For instance, we have, under the New Grants Framework, supported arts practitioners and organisations to engage and collaborate with communities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Kok mentioned the ArtsWok Collective, which NAC's Seed Grant proudly founded.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The group, together with Drama Box, worked closely with patients, caregivers and healthcare professionals from Khoo Teck Puat Hospital to produce a series of artworks, inviting the public to reflect on and share their thoughts on the culturally-sensitive issues of death and dying.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I agree with Mr Kok Heng Leun on the importance of intermediaries for the growth of community arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These grants allow them to focus on their professional development and to produce high quality programmes that can better reach out to their various beneficiaries and target audiences.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun also spoke about setting appropriate targets for arts groups.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We can assure him that the objectives for Major and Seed Grant companies are customised to reflect the companies' vision, target audience and programmes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example, a performing arts company's KPIs could include audience outreach at their performances and training workshops for practitioners, while an intermediary's KPIs would also consider the quality of the experience rather than just outreach numbers alone.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun also pointed out that a space does not simply become a place without support from the local community and we recognise the importance of creative place-making being relational and ground-up.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Minister Grace Fu shared our plans to continue investing in programming and marketing efforts to revitalise the Bras Basah-Bugis precinct and the Civic District.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: And this needs to go hand in hand with community ownership and strong support from the arts and heritage groups within the areas.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We are just starting out on this journey to involve local communities in our place-making efforts and we encourage both artists and arts groups and intermediaries, as well as residents and community stakeholders to step forward, collaborate with one another to build and develop the character of local precincts around the island.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked how we are stepping up efforts to support traditional arts, facilitate cross-cultural understanding and help Singapore better appreciate our roots.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We are, indeed, looking at ways to uplift the traditional arts sector and keep traditional arts relevant and accessible to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue to professionalise and nurture the next generation of traditional arts talent.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Many of the arts organisations supported by NAC's Major Grant Scheme have a strong focus on developing quality traditional arts programmes and are also actively reaching out to the community.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: An example is Apsaras Arts, a former recipient of NAC's Seed Grant and now Major Grant.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Besides creating works and staging performances, Apsaras Arts also started DEVATA – Friends of Apsaras Arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It is a tiered membership programme to reach out to the community and corporates so that it can grow sustainably and consolidate a fan base.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Apsaras also established Dance India Asia Pacific, an intensive programme where students develop their techniques in Indian classical dance, taught by renowned international practitioners.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Another example is NADI Singapura, a traditional Malay drums and percussion company that was also supported by NAC's Seed and now Major Grant.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NADI was founded by 31-year-old Riduan Zalani, who seeks to push the boundaries of traditional music by infusing modern elements Page: 41 in his works.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: More importantly, Riduan, also a recipient of last year's National Young Artist Award, hopes to spread the love of traditional arts to other young musicians and audiences.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: To identify and encourage potential musical talents in the traditional arts sector, NAC organises the triennial National Indian Music Competition and biennial National Chinese Music Competition.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These competitions enable musicians in Singapore to develop their performing skills and raise their musical standards and provide opportunities for musicians to perform in a competitive environment.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NAC also has a Malay music enrichment course that was developed for Malay practitioners who do not have the benefit of formal music training.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: (In Mandarin):   To reach out to a broader audience, we want to raise the visibility of traditional arts through key community and artistic platforms.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example, at last year's Mid-Autumn Festival celebrations at Gardens by the Bay, traditional arts groups, like Dicapella Dizi Ensemble and Nam Hwa Opera, put up nightly cultural shows for 10 days.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NAC will continue to work with Gardens by the Bay to showcase traditional arts performances at this year's festival.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: If you dropped by River Hongbao this year, you may also remember the lively 乖小丑 performance by the young students of Sheng Hong Arts Institute.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: They are adorable and full of energy, so it is no wonder why the performance was so well-received.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I think we can and should find more platforms for traditional arts performers to showcase their talents to an even wider audience.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: That is why we are also working with companies, such as Singapore Hokkien Huay Kuan Dance Theatre, Era Dance Theatre and Ding Yi Music Company, to bring their signature traditional arts programmes to the heartlands and closer to residents.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: To reach out to younger audiences, we will be commissioning traditional arts groups to produce traditional arts programmes with interactive elements to be staged in schools.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NAC is currently working with Traditional Arts Centre to develop an original and age-appropriate Chinese opera production to perform at different schools.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We are also piloting a series of bite-sized programmes by local and regional arts companies customised for pre-schools and primary schools to deepen our young Singaporeans' understanding of our multicultural society during Racial Harmony Day in July.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We hope that through these initiatives, we can help our younger ones better enjoy and appreciate traditional arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: (In English): Mdm Chair, besides major festivals and programmes in schools, NAC is also partnering the National Museum of Singapore to establish a dedicated space within the museum where digital media will be used to provide an immersive environment for visitors to engage with traditional arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue to find new ways to engage Singaporeans, especially our digital-savvy youths, whether in sports, arts or heritage.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The digital space is one that cuts across boundaries.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: During the SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games last year, we saw how a simple hashtag like #OneTeamSG could connect Singaporeans separated physically, but united in their support for and pride of our athletes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: And we will continue to tap on digital spaces and social media platforms to encourage live participation and interaction, whether you are at a sports centre, gallery or museum.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Page: 42 To complement visits to our museums and reach out to a wider audience, NHB will be launching its new Heritage Portal, Roots.sg.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Besides providing access to our entire national collection online, Roots.sg presents heritage resources in a much more dynamic manner.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, if you are a teacher preparing to bring your students on a heritage trail in Kampong Glam, check out Roots.sg.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: You can view the sites and monuments on the trail, click on links to find out more about the history and download worksheets for your students.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Your students, too, can watch videos of traditional trades in Kampong Glam and do further research after the excursion.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, whether you are a serious researcher or just a curious young student, Roots.sg will provide a new dimension for you to explore and learn more about our history and heritage.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Ms Alex Yam and Ms Rahayu Mahzam spoke about making arts and culture accessible to young children, especially those from lower-income families.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Senior Minister of State spoke about the ArtReach programme, which aims to build a more inclusive community through arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I agree that we should expose children to arts and culture early so that we can better help them develop creativity and confidence.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Soka Kindergarten, for instance, worked with Kavanagh Dance on an Artist-in-School Scheme project to help teachers integrate dance and movement into the school's curriculum.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This was a rare but enriching experience for the Soka Kindergarten teachers to collaborate with artists like Ms Gloria Soh in the classroom and to help their students gain confidence through music and dance.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This is a partnership between artists and teachers as they seek to incorporate the arts more holistically in a preschool environment.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The arts experience in schools will continue to be supplemented with children- and family-friendly programming at our arts institutions.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In July last year, for instance, the Aliwal Arts Centre organised the third edition of its Aliwal Arts Night Crawl, a family- and youth-centric festival.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: One of the popular activities was Uncle Rajah's Flying Carpet Tales, a mesmerising Singaporean folk tale story-telling session by Chris Mooney-Singh of Word Forward, otherwise known as Uncle Rajah.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Parents can look forward to spending quality time together with their kids through a variety of multi-disciplinary arts programmes, including dance, music and theatre performances and story-telling sessions.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Through arts, heritage and sports, there are plenty of opportunities for all of us to be involved even in the heartlands.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We Page: 43 will continue to nurture and develop talents in arts and sports, even from a very young age.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This is a nation of resilient communities, a cohesive and caring society of engaged citizens and, most importantly, a Singapore that Singaporeans are proud to call home.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have a bit of time for clarifications.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I hope that the Ministry can roll out more publicity materials as well as how to encourage more people from a more diverse walk of life to apply for Our Singapore Fund.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The second clarification is on our art scene in terms of National Gallery and museum visits.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Is there going to be a programme in place, like what we are going to do with OBS?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Are we going to have a programme with MOE to get all students to have a chance to visit our museums and galleries somewhere within the 12 years of their formal education?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are very keen to see it extended beyond that and will work very hard to justify the Fund.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To us, to have enthusiastic participation from as many wide-ranging groups as possible is our objective.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I would like to assure the Member that we are totally in line with his recommendation to have greater publicity so that all sectors of the community know about it and will come forward to tap on the Fund.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But the local numbers are the ones that have been growing quite encouragingly.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: My direction to colleagues in NHB and the art institutions is make our world-class facilities and collections speak to the population.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I totally agree with Members who said if it is just hardware, it will remain hardware.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To me, the success will be decided as to whether our collections can speak to two segments of the population.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Because I think the elder generation requires, sometimes, a vernacular interpretation, requires some more thoughtful guidance of the exhibition.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, if we are able to attract more of them to return, I think we would have made the museum experience meaningful for them.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Recently, I accompanied a group of residents to the National Art Gallery.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But I think many of them were quite daunted by the steps that they had to navigate.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As you know, it is quite a big structure over quite a large extensive area.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I have asked my museum colleagues to see how we can tailor a programme that brings them to as many Page: 44 noteworthy artworks with as economic use of steps as possible.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The other segment is the children because, to me, that is the generation that we need to reach out to.

text: It is developing the next generation of audience.

text: We need to present art in a different way that will make it appealing to them.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Given their limited life experience and the context that they are in, we need to bring art education to a different level.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, that is the priority given to my colleagues.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have two clarifications for the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)

text: We are glad to hear that MOE is moving away from grades and looking at different types of scoring.

text: Certainly, it is in our interest and the interest of the community to get as many as possible onto the registration system because it gives our community, both parents and institutions, a wide selection of asatizahs whom we feel will understand the local context and who can teach Islam to our students.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is good for our students not only to have a good grasp of the knowledge but also be a part of modern Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The Minister talked about using art for the purposes of unity, harmony and comments.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Any society is not just based on that; it is also about discord, dissensus as well as, a lot of times, disagreement.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: So, what does the Minister think about providing that safe space so that we can have diversity?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I just want to remind the House that John F Kennedy did say, "If we cannot end now our differences, at least we can help make the world safe for diversity".

text: Based on what I hear, most of the engagements for place-making tend to be top-down.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Quite often, traditional arts is about trying new things.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Li Yu in his book "Sketches of Idle Pleasure" (闲情偶寄) talked about "thinking out of the box" in length, in other words, only by creating new things can we communicate with the audience.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The process of "thinking out of the box" also takes time.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Members, I would really like to be democratic and today is the last day.

speaker: The Chairman
text: But please do not make speeches during clarification time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I do agree that in art, we look for opportunities where we can have discourse.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think art has that potential of allowing the expression of opinions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But we also need to recognise that art has this ability to evoke emotions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think artists want to see that their work has that ability to influence and to affect.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Creating a space where certain segments, perhaps the more mature, perhaps those able to deal with the issue, can be engaged in that discourse.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Artworks that were not shown in the past, now have been shown regularly, including some of the forum theatre work that Mr Kok himself is so closely associated with.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I hope that the arts community will give the regulator acknowledgement that it has happened.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Having said that, as I have explained earlier on, we do need regulations in order to maintain a common space that is as wide as possible, so that people, the audience and the artists can engage in art making and art appreciation in a safe environment.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On the second question about place-making, some parts of it may seem to be top-down initially, but it has evolved.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think PA PAssionArts, when it first started, was top-down.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We needed to have some organised activities; we needed to provide some training; we needed to decide what was the theme and so on, because it was something new.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But without a push from the agencies, probably we may not have been able to develop it as quickly as we would have liked.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Page: 47 But over time, you have seen certain local communities embracing a project and making it their own.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They are putting in their themes; they are staking their claim; they are deciding what to be depicted, what to be portrayed.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: With the local community stepping forward, agencies like PA would gladly step back and let the locals have greater decision-making.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Also in some projects, we have deliberately assigned the job to a theatre production professional.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SIFA is actually undertaken by Mr Ong Keng Sen who is not part of the agency.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That is a way for an art practitioner to take a leading role in curating and in assisting the Government in producing works for the public to enjoy.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Although it is top-down in the sense that the Government is coming up with the funding, but the actual production, organisation, commissioning work are actually done by someone from the private sector.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I will leave Parliamentary Secretary Baey to address the question on traditional arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This is because the arts, especially traditional arts, need to be supported and enjoyed by the audience.

text: So, in this aspect, I hope traditional arts groups can put more thought into cultivating their audiences.

text: Not long ago, I attended a performance by Sheng Hong Arts Institute and got to know their artistic director.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: She is a young lady whose mother is a traditional Chinese dance practitioner.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: She is an NAC scholarship recipient and went overseas to study.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: After coming back, she became Sheng Hong's artistic director.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I noticed that their students are of different age groups, including some very adorable children who are keen to learn traditional Chinese dance.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It is truly encouraging to see so many young people and children who like traditional arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NAC will continue to support the development of traditional arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I hope that Singapore audiences will also support our traditional arts practitioners.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In recent weeks, we have seen certain incidents affecting the Malay/Muslim communities, such as the attacks on the madrasah students as well as the incident with the management of a mall, Tampines One.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I have read with concern the comments online following these events.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Some from the Malay/Muslim community have also shared their concerns about discrimination against the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There will always be pockets of people who, either through no fault of theirs or a mistake in terms of miscommunication, or, as in the case of the madrasah student, we have read reports that the person is a bit mentally Page: 48 challenged.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: While these events can never be prevented 100%, the most important thing is to see the reaction.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: What heartens me most was that a lot of Singaporeans came onboard and condemned those acts and they are from all races and all backgrounds.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We know that multiracialism, respect for differences in Singapore, the ability to stay united for the last 50 years, are an important part of our existence as a small nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We cherish it and we have to work hard at it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: My take on it is that it is something which we should never condone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We should try and work together to prevent it from happening.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The responses were very good to show a maturity that sometimes you cannot find in other societies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the case of both incidents, you also find Singaporean Chinese coming forward condemning the act.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, it goes to show that we understand what is right and what is wrong.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To the second question on what it is that we can do to tackle this problem, it is about integration, about coming together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Recently, Minister Shanmugam also asked for non-Malay Singaporeans to reach out.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We know that integration is a two-way process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: You can see the various efforts, not just by the Inter-Religious Organisation but the bottom-up movement in the community, in the constituencies, for people who want to reach out to one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Earlier in my speech, I have responded that I think it is something we should have to inculcate from a very young age – a curiosity for others, to know who the people are around us, who are our neighbours, who are our friends.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: If there is another incident, we are all responsible to condemn it and work together at it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Well, look at the history of America, 200 years old and they still have problems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is a work-in-progress but the most important thing is that everyone must see that this is their responsibility to prevent it from happening.

text: They want to do things on their own.
